page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes equipped with 161 GB of local SSD temporary storage, while graphic accelerators are absent.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core reaching the top 25 percent and a Geekbench single-core score of 1501.0. However, multi-core and aggregate throughput benchmarks reflect its 4-vCPU footprint, recording weaker relative scores in multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core (3353.0), and PassMark CPU ratings. Memory subsystem testing shows average PassMark memory results and single-threaded gzip compression, though raw read and write memory bandwidth fell into lower percentiles. Cryptographic operations remain solid due to hardware support for AES, VAES, and SHA extensions.

Given its resource profile and dedicated allocation, the D4ads_v5 provides reliable baseline computational efficiency for small-to-medium business services without overpaying for enterprise-scale core counts. The included 161 GB local SSD offers low-latency scratch space useful for caching and temporary data stores. This configuration is well matched for mid-tier web serving, build and test pipelines, microservices, application staging environments, and lightweight database instances that operate effectively within a 16 GB memory boundary.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of memory, and 161 GB of local SSD temporary storage, it provides a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio without discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core CPU throughput, reaching the top 25 percent in stress-ng single-thread tests, accompanied by average single-threaded compression and cryptographic performance. Multi-core compute and memory bandwidth are limited by the four-thread ceiling, reflecting lower tier results in multi-threaded benchmarks and Redis operations. The bundled local solid-state disk provides fast local scratch space, making the instance an effective choice for general workloads including web application hosting, continuous integration runners, lightweight caching servers, and intermediate data staging tasks.
